instrument: Ordinance No. O-26-26, moratorium on development applications for data centers (enacted Sept 21, 2026)
summary: Adopted 5-1 on third reading Sept 21, 2026: a 12-month moratorium on data centers above 65 IT megawatts of combined electrical load (excluding ancillary equipment and power serving other businesses). Below that, a data center is exempt only if located in a named industrial park or former industrial site and not self-generating except emergency backup; exempt projects must submit light, glare, noise and landscaping plans, sit at least one mile from another data center, and enter a development agreement. Ancillary server rooms and crypto mining are excluded; projects with a development permit in the prior 12 months (Valara) are unaffected.

source.citation: WSPA, Fox Carolina, Post and Courier (Sept 21-26, 2026)

notes: CORRECTION: prior versions described a >65 MW threshold (Sept 22) and then the unamended first-reading text (Sept 24 load). Enacted text read in original. Changes from first reading: definition now excludes ancillary server rooms/IT closets and digital asset mining; development-permit exemption lookback is 18 months (first reading said 12). Readings: first June 22, second and public hearing July 20, third Sept 21, 2026. Pending Ordinance Doctrine applied from first reading. Opposed at third reading: Coker (reported). Council reconvened Sept 25 and voted to reconsider third reading; a press attorney says that meeting was illegal and the Sept 21 version stands. The county's posted summary differs from what passed.
confidence_note: Adopted text not read. CORRECTION: the earlier version read in the original (1 MW combined connected load, blanket pause) was superseded on third reading.
